newsitem.title: UK: BAe merges own naval systems into BAeSEMA.
newsitem.headline: BAe merges own naval systems into BAeSEMA.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc said on Monday it had agreed with Sema Group to consolidate BAe's main naval systems business into their existing joint venture company, BAeSEMA.

"BAeSEMA will act as the focal point for pursuing both naval whole ship prime contracts and their existing naval systems business," the aerospace company said in a statement, adding the move would strenghten the venture and its competitive position.

BAeSEMA counts specialist naval design, software and systems skills among its existing activities, but BAe managing director John Weston said this restructuring would add into the joint venture BAe's "broader prime contracting and systems skills".
Last year BAe's main British defence contracting rival GEC Plc won a prolonged takeover battle with BAe for VSEL, a naval submarine and shipyard based in northern England.
The move left GEC dominating a sector in which BAe has ambitions but no large British shipyard of its own. The other main national competitor is Vosper Thornycroft.
